_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Level tiles: outline only on your level, dots on phones; readout and ? tweaks
detail: Level tiles (everywhere): only the selected tile has an outline (red).
Phones: each tile shows one dot in its least-learned colour (any new → white, else any seen → yellow, else green) instead of a thin bar.
Phones: 'Level' and 'Words 1–100' a step larger; the ? sits at the right edge, level with the section title.
Example words and coverage line use the same font as the level readout (DM Sans), in the dimmer grey.

entries.summary: About is its own page: opens in a new tab, looks the same for everyone, never touches sign-in
detail: Sidebar About, Settings → About and Help → More about this project open #/about in a new tab instead of over the app.
#/about never reads your account or starts sign-in, so it looks the same signed in or not.
Removed 'Back to the app (name)', the 'Back to app' pill, and the × that showed for visitors even though it did nothing.
The 'Welcome back / Continue session' box is no longer built on the About page.

entries.summary: Practise is hidden until you've answered your first card; Learn alone before that
detail: Never answered anything: the home screen is Learn only (no Practise column on desktop, no folded Practise row on phones). Removes the 'Nothing to practise yet' text.
After any answer, Practise appears and stays, showing 'All caught up' and the next due time when empty.
Desktop (1360px+): Learn alone is centred at 980px instead of stretched across the screen.

entries.summary: Desktop sidebar: Tutorial and About icons are a plain ? and i (no circle)
detail: Desktop sidebar only; the phone top bar keeps its circled ? beside the other line icons.

entries.summary: Function words no longer split into companion cards (a, se, os, as, nos, pela): one card per word
detail: A function word's back lists every construction already, so its companion cards showed the same rows twice.
Portuguese: 619 -> 612 cards; each of those words is now one card with its word-type pills on the front, like que.
Spanish function words not checked.

entries.summary: Phone top bar tighter and larger; folded Learn shows only its level; plain ? help; 'Mistakes first' hint
detail: Phone top bar: about 8px higher, the line 6px under the icons (was 18px); flag 25→29px, language name 16→18px, icons 26→29px.
Phone: with Practise open, folded Learn shows only 'Level N · Words X–Y' (no bar or counts).
Phone: leaf and clock icons sit beside 'Learn' and 'Practise'; the ? is small and raised after the title, and only on the open section.
Everywhere: the section help is a plain ? (no circle).
Practise hint: 'Mistakes first', shown only when there are both mistakes and words to review.

entries.summary: Function-word cards: pattern and meaning read left to right on one row, and the function word is just bold (no grey highlight)
detail: Each pattern row is left-aligned: the pattern (e.g. 'verb + de') on the left, its meaning ('of, about') on the right of the same row.
When a pattern and its meaning don't fit on one line, the meaning drops beneath, left-aligned. If any row on a card needs that, all rows on that card do, so the card stays uniform.
The grey wash behind the function word in the pattern rows and the example sentence is gone; it is bold white only.

entries.summary: Card back: a word whose shown senses cover little of its usage now shows more of them, instead of a '6 rarer senses' line (novo)
detail: Hidden senses are promoted, biggest first, until the shown ones cover 60% of the word's sense usage. Each must be at least 10% of that usage and have an example; at most three are added.
Portuguese, first 619 cards: six change (por +1, bem +2, ficar +1, qualquer +1, novo +2, sério +1). novo now reads 'new' with two contexts, and 'young'.
The '6 rarer senses' row stays in the code for cards that still qualify for it, which should now be very few.
Checked in the app on novo (dark mode); the other five were counted, not viewed. Spanish and the other languages were not scanned.

entries.summary: Card back: a shared translation's rows no longer repeat the shared context (daqui: 'of' over two rows, no 'in relation to ·' prefix)
detail: When the rows under a shared translation also shared a context, each row still started with it. A row now shows only its own context; a row with nothing of its own shows the shared words, so none is empty.
daqui: 'of' over '· introduces the name of a place following its hypernym' and '· in relation to'.
Checked in the app on daqui (dark mode). Not re-checked: só, other languages.

entries.summary: Card back: a card opens with only the word type in use expanded; contexts under a shared translation take a bullet
detail: The other word types open as their word-type row (translation beside the pill), the same way they look after you tap a sub-meaning, instead of opening fully expanded and then folding on the first tap.
Each context row under a shared translation starts with the same dot that sits between translation and context elsewhere; a wrapped line hangs under the text.
A shared grammar frame ('+ a / para' on deu) stays beside the heading rather than repeating on every row.
Checked in the app on merda, sé, una, daqui and deu (dark mode). Light mode and phone width not checked.

entries.summary: Card back: an empty word-type row is small again; the coloured edge shows only on the word type in use
detail: A word-type row is the taller, larger-text size only when it holds the shared translation; otherwise it is back to its 36px size.
The coloured left edge on a word-type row you are not on is no longer drawn.
Checked in the app on una (dark mode): 36px rows, edge only on the verb. The taller size on a row with a shared translation was not re-checked.

entries.summary: Card back: the word-type row you are not on has no grey tint
detail: The faint grey band on a word-type row (Adjective on una while you are on the verb) is gone, so only the word type in use looks marked. Its coloured left edge and pill stay.
Checked in the app on una (dark mode). Light mode and phone width not checked.

entries.summary: Card back: a shared translation shows alone until it is chosen; a family shares a translation or a context, not both
detail: An unchosen shared translation (daqui: 'of') is one line; its contexts open when you choose it. This applies within one word type too, not only between word types.

When sub-rows shared a translation and also a context (daqui: 'of' and 'in relation to'), the context is no longer lifted into the heading. Each row keeps it: 'in relation to · introduces the name of a place…' and 'in relation to', instead of a leftover reading 'general use'.
Checked in the app on daqui (dark mode). Not checked: light mode, phone width, the Spanish shared-context groups, or cards with several shared translations in one word type.

entries.summary: Card back: the grammar frame (+ que, + com) shows only on the row in use, as a pill with the phrase (contar que)
detail: The frame sits at the end of the row in use's context line, as a quiet pill holding the whole phrase ('contar que', 'acreditar em'). Other rows drop it, so they take no extra width.
A row that is only a frame (estar: '+ em', '+ adj') is left as it was.
Checked in the app on contar, acredito and estar (dark mode). Not checked: light mode, phone width, grouped rows (there are no longer any with frames in the Portuguese cards I scanned).

entries.summary: Card back: senses only share a heading when their whole list of translations is the same (contar, acredito stay as plain rows)
detail: A sense with two translations ('to tell; to narrate') no longer joins one that is only 'to tell' under a shared 'to tell'. It keeps its translations together on its own row.
Portuguese, first 619 cards: shared-translation groups go from 136 to 87, and none has a sub-row with an extra translation.
Applies to every language that groups by translation.

entries.summary: Card back: shared contexts and frames only move up into the word-type row for the word type in use; shared translations still do wherever there's room
detail: On a word type you aren't on, a shared context (or grammar frame) stays in its rows instead of taking up the word-type row. Shared translations still go up so you can see them at a glance.
A word type whose group shares both a translation and a context stays as it was (nothing moves up) until you are on it.

Checked on the Portuguese cards: inactive word types with a shared translation still show it in the header (merda, sé, poder). No Portuguese card has an inactive word type with a shared context, so that branch was not seen on a real card.

entries.summary: Card back: a sub-row under a shared translation stays left-aligned when it wraps (deu)
detail: A long sub-row (deu: 'to transfer one's possession of something to someone...') centred its wrapped lines while the short ones sat left. All lines are now left-aligned under a shared translation.

entries.summary: Card back: shared context moves into the rows when it fits (up · higher); translations beside a shared heading are inflected too (I think)
detail: A group that shares a context over two or more translations (arriba: higher over up, above) shows 'up · higher' and 'above · higher' when each fits on one line, instead of a caption line plus one line each. If any would wrap, the caption stays.
acredito: the heading read 'I believe' but the translation beside it read 'to think'. Translations next to a shared heading now take the same form, so it reads 'I think'.
Only Spanish cards have shared-context groups (none in the first 619 Portuguese cards), so the first change was checked on a hand-built row, not on the real arriba card.

entries.summary: Card back: no outlines on sense and sub-meaning rows that aren't chosen; pressing the word-type row selects the whole group again
detail: Resting rows have no border and no tint; the chosen row is the fill plus left edge. A faint wash shows on hover.

When a word type carries its group's shared words (estar: to be), pressing that row selects every sub-meaning at once, so you can go from one sub-meaning back to all. Pressing it again folds the section as before.
Grouped rows with the shared text inside the group already did this; unchanged.

entries.summary: Card back: the chosen sub-meaning is one marker, its whole row as a rounded rectangle with a left edge (no chip round the text)
detail: Replaces the row wash plus text chip: the active sub-meaning row now has a 0.24 fill and the 4px left edge of a sense row, with the text unchanged and still on its column.
Both layouts: shared text in the word-type row (água, aún) and shared text in the group row (dejar, passar).

entries.summary: Card back: the chosen sub-meaning's whole row is washed in the one-grouped-row layout too (água, aún)
detail: The wash across the chosen sub-meaning's row only worked for groups whose shared text stays in the group row (dejar); in the layout where the shared text moves up to the word-type row (água, aún, realmente) a higher-priority rule kept the row transparent, so only the text was highlighted. Both layouts now wash the row.

entries.summary: Card back: grammar frames are inline everywhere; a sub-row's gloss and context share a line (guerra: warfare · the waging of war)
detail: The base grammar-frame rule was a full-width flex block from the older layout; it is now inline, so no wrapper can reintroduce a line break after a short gloss.
A sub-row's own gloss ('warfare') was a block that pushed its context ('the waging of war') onto a second line even when both fit; they now read 'warfare · the waging of war' on one line.

entries.summary: Card back: a grammar frame after a translation (you know +inf) stays on the translation's line
detail: The frame was drawn as a full-width block under the gloss, so a short gloss and a short frame used two lines. It is now inline, so 'you know +inf' is one line; longer ones still wrap.

entries.summary: Card back: removed the stray empty line under rows that have only a gloss and a grammar cue (e.g. Portuguese sabes)
detail: An empty, already-hoisted context span was still being drawn as an inline block and wrapped onto its own blank line; the rule that hides it now wins over the rule that showed it.
Affects any single-gloss row whose context was hoisted away; sabes rows shrink from about 94px to 68px.

entries.summary: Card back: word-type rows are always larger; the chosen sub-meaning keeps a light wash over its whole row
detail: Every word-type row (Verb, Noun...) is now 20px text and 44px high, like a sense row, whether or not it holds shared text.
The active sub-meaning keeps a light wash across its whole row as well as the rounded highlight on its text.

entries.summary: Card back: grouped senses whose shared text stays in the group row (dejar) get the same left column and rounded active marker; word-type row is larger
detail: dejar: 'to leave' stays centred over a left-aligned column of to put / to forget / to bequeath; the chosen one is a rounded rectangle just left of the column and the group drops to a light wash.
Shared-context groups (eh) get a bracketed left-aligned caption over centred translations.
The word-type row, when it holds the shared translation, is now 20px and 44px high like a sense row.

entries.summary: Card back: active sub-meaning is a rounded rectangle sized to its text; shared-text header and sub-rows never share an alignment
detail: Active sub-meaning (aún: still / yet) now uses the same rounded fill + left-edge rectangle as a sense row, sized to its own text, instead of a ring around the whole row.
Shared context is a bracketed caption beside the word type, with the translations centred below it.
Shared translation is centred across the whole word-type row, with its contexts in a left-aligned column and the marker just left of the active line.
Inactive sub-rows lose their boxes inside this layout.

entries.summary: Card back: when a whole group of meanings is selected, its rows read as one block
detail: With a shared translation or context over several sub-meanings (aún: time over still / yet) and none chosen, the rows now share one fill and one left bar, with hairlines between them, instead of looking like separate selected rows.
Tapping a single sub-meaning returns to the row-by-row marker.

entries.summary: Function-word cards: the active pattern uses the same fill-and-left-bar marker as other senses
detail: The selected pattern box on function-word backs (de, que, em...) now has a 0.24 fill and a 4px left bar in its partner's colour instead of a 2px outline.

entries.summary: Card back: the active sense is marked by a stronger fill and a left bar instead of an outline
detail: The active sense row (and the active sub-meaning inside a grouped sense) now has a 0.24 fill and a 4px bar on its left edge in its word type's colour; the 2px outline is gone.
Applies to single rows, grouped rows, and the group that is lit when several word types are on the card; dark and light theme.
Inactive rows and the word-type rows are unchanged.
